q: 84 tins are shared equally among 4 boxes. How many tins go in each box?
hint: Which amount is being shared, and how many equal shares are needed (4)?
error_note: The fixed total 84 is being shared into 4 equal parts. Divide it rather than multiplying.

subject: maths
q: A trip has 146 pupils and 9 adults. Each minibus has 12 passenger seats. How many minibuses are needed?

steps.title: Divide by the passenger seats in each minibus
steps.note: Twelve minibuses fill up, with eleven people still needing seats.

steps.title: Allow one more minibus for the remaining people
steps.note: Everyone must travel, so round the number of minibuses up.

hint: How many people need seats, including the 9 adults? After dividing by 12, decide what any remainder means.
method_note: Add the pupils and adults, divide by the seats per minibus, then allow one more minibus for the remaining people.
check: 12 × 12 = 144 seats is too few for 155 people; 13 × 12 = 156 seats is enough.
error_note: Twelve minibuses provide only 144 seats. The remaining eleven people need another minibus.

subject: maths
q: 145 students need minibuses with 9 passenger seats each. Hire costs £40 per minibus. Find the total cost.

steps.title: Divide to find whole groups and the remainder
steps.note: 16 complete groups of 9, with 1 left over.

steps.title: Answer the question in context
steps.note: Everyone or everything needs a place; add one group when there is a remainder.

steps.title: Use the intermediate result
steps.note: Find the total for these equal groups.

hint: If some are left after making groups of 9, do they still need a place? What will that first result represent?
method_note: 16 complete groups of 9, with 1 left over. Everyone or everything needs a place; add one group when there is a remainder. Find the total for these equal groups.
error_note: 16 groups of 9 have only 144 places. Include one more group before multiplying by £40.
source: Accepted M03 source slide 1; saved deck text checked
